outcomes.text: Read and understand a wide range of 19th-century non-fiction, including whole texts and unseen texts.
Identify and interpret themes, ideas and information in literature and other high-quality writing.
Read in different ways for different purposes and judge how useful, relevant and well presented the content is.
Draw inferences and back them with evidence; support a point of view by referring to the text.
Spot bias and misuse of evidence, telling supported statements from unsupported ones.
Reflect critically on a text using its context and wider reading, and recognise that responses can differ.
Identify main themes and summarise ideas and information from a single text.
Explain how vocabulary and grammar create effect and impact, using linguistic terms accurately.
Analyse and evaluate how form and structure make a text effective.
Write accurately and effectively to describe, narrate, explain, instruct, inform, respond and argue for different audiences.
Choose vocabulary, grammar, form and structure to suit audience, purpose and context.
Use language imaginatively, use information from others, keep a consistent viewpoint and keep the text coherent.
Select, organise and emphasise facts, ideas and key points, and support views with well-chosen evidence or quotation.
Create emotional impact and use persuasive language and rhetorical devices such as rhetorical questions, antithesis and parenthesis.
Write a transactional text in this form: article or blog.
Write a transactional text in this form: formal email or letter.
Write a transactional text in this form: report or review.
Write a transactional text in this form: text for a speech.
Write a transactional text in this form: section of a guide, leaflet or booklet.

subtopics.title: Reading modern prose and literary non-fiction

outcomes.text: Read and understand a wide range of 20th- and 21st-century prose fiction and literary non-fiction, including unseen texts.
Identify and interpret themes, ideas and information in literature and other high-quality writing.
Read in different ways for different purposes and judge how useful, relevant and well presented the content is.
Draw inferences and back them with evidence; support a point of view by referring to the text.
Reflect critically on a text using its context and wider reading, and recognise that responses can differ.
Identify main themes, summarise a single text and synthesise ideas from more than one text.
Compare two or more texts critically on themes, ideas, evidence and response.
Write accurately and effectively to describe, narrate, explain, instruct, inform, respond and argue for different audiences.
Choose vocabulary, grammar, form and structure to suit audience, purpose and context.
Use language imaginatively, use information from others, keep a consistent viewpoint and keep the text coherent.
Select, organise and emphasise facts, ideas and key points, and support views with well-chosen evidence or quotation.
Create emotional impact and use persuasive language and rhetorical devices such as rhetorical questions, antithesis and parenthesis.
Use the writer's craft seen in fiction reading to inspire and shape imaginative writing, with planning and proofreading.
Select and organise ideas persuasively for a prepared talk, planning for purpose and audience.
Listen to and respond appropriately to questions and feedback.
Express ideas in spoken Standard English where appropriate.
